done_when: Table per approach class (near-miss, wick-through, close-through-then-fail 1st/2nd close, accepted) x TF with n, forward move, and the confirm sequence + invalidation sequence that best separated outcomes, as measured base rates (descriptive, fee-free, labelled); dev/holdout split before any rule is proposed; result feeds the live_aid probability panel.
goal: Learn how to trade an approach to a dominant lower high (Krown KR-L10; operator's daily line) or prior-day high as a thesis: anticipate at the approach, list the next things that must happen if the thesis is right (in order, with time limits), and the things that prove it wrong (= exit). Measure on Binance BTC history which layer sequences after an approach (OI, CVD, net delta, closes per TF, daily BB mid, other levels nearby) separated the approaches that failed from the ones that broke, and how often (probability with n).
note: Operator 10-30: 'We cannot work with certainties. We can only work with probabilities. And probability is going to be our edge ... if I have anticipated this, then these are the next things that must happen before I can say that okay, my understanding was wrong. And this is when I have to get out of the trade.'
title: level-approach study: daily 'last lower high' line (operator definition: highest high since the leg that made the latest lower low, e.g. 82,035 from 10-23) and prior-day highs; classify every approach as near-miss / wick-through-close-back / close-through-then-fail (1st, 2nd close) / accepted, per 1m 5m 15m 1h close, with OI, CVD, net delta, RSI, daily BB mid at the moment and forward move; Binance BTC history; descriptive first
